articles.title: Diwali 2026 Puja Guide: Puja Vidhi, Laxmi Pooja Shubh Muhurat, Mantras, and everything you need to know
articles.summary: Ask anyone what Diwali looks like and you’ll hear about diyas on the windowsill, rangoli at the door, new clothes, boxes of mithai and relatives crowding
articles.body: Ask anyone what Diwali looks like and you’ll hear about diyas on the windowsill, rangoli at the door, new clothes, boxes of mithai and relatives crowding into one living room. All of that is real. But under the sparkle sits an older idea that people keep coming back to every year: light wins over darkness, knowledge over ignorance, and hope over despair. It’s one of the biggest festivals in India, and for many families it’s the time of year to ask for blessings, welcome prosperity and start fresh.This year Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026. The main focus is the worship of Goddess Lakshmi, who is associated with wealth and well-being, together with Lord Ganesha, the one who clears obstacles from our path. Below is a plain walkthrough of why the festival is celebrated, when to do the puja, how to do it, and which mantras go with which day.Why do we celebrate Diwali?The word Deepawali comes from two Sanskrit words: deepa, meaning lamp, and avali, meaning row. So the name literally describes what you see on the festival night, long lines of small flames lighting up homes, lanes and public spaces.The best-known story comes from the Ramayana. After fourteen years in exile, and after defeating Ravana, Lord Rama came back to Ayodhya with Sita and Lakshmana. The city welcomed them by lighting earthen lamps along their path, and the custom has survived ever since.That’s only one version, though. Different regions and communities hold different stories close. Some link the day to Lord Krishna’s victory over the demon Narakasura. Others see it mainly as the day to honour Lakshmi and begin a new, hopeful chapter. What they share is the sense of good prevailing over bad.There’s a quieter lesson in it too. Prosperity isn’t only about money. Good health, people who care about you, a sense of contentment and the sense to spend wisely all count, and Diwali is a decent moment to remember that.Lakshmi Puja Shubh Muhurat and Amavasya timingsAccording to Drik Panchang, Lakshmi-Ganesha Puja is traditionally done during Pradosh Kaal, the period after sunset, while the Amavasya Tithi is in effect. Many astrologers also suggest choosing a fixed Lagna, which is believed to be favourable for worshipping Lakshmi.The fixed Lagna windows listed for November 8, 2026 are:Kumbha Lagna (Aquarius): 01:18 PM to 02:55 PMVrishabha Lagna (Taurus): 06:12 PM to 08:12 PMSimha Lagna (Leo): 12:38 AM to 02:47 AM on November 9The Amavasya Tithi starts at 11:27 AM on November 8 and ends at 12:31 PM on November 9.For most households, the Vrishabha Lagna is the one that matters, because it overlaps with Pradosh Kaal. That makes the early evening, roughly 6:12 PM to 8:12 PM, the window most families aim for. Tradition names four fixed signs for this puja: Vrishchika, Kumbha, Vrishabha and Simha. The belief is that worship done in a fixed Lagna brings steadier, longer-lasting prosperity.One caution: these timings are for Manwat, India, as published by Drik Panchang. Muhurat times shift from place to place, so check a local Panchang for your own city before you sit down for the puja.Diwali puja vidhi: how to worship Lakshmi and GaneshaLakshmi Puja is the heart of the festival. It’s done to ask for happiness, good fortune and wellbeing for the household.Most of the preparation happens before the evening. People clean the house thoroughly, since a tidy home is considered the right way to invite Lakshmi in, then decorate the entrance with rangoli, flowers and diyas.Here’s a simple outline of the puja itself:Set up the puja space. Clear a clean platform or chowki and place idols or pictures of Lakshmi and Ganesha on it.Gather the samagri. Keep flowers, fruits, sweets, incense, a diya, rice, kumkum and sandalwood paste within reach, along with any other offerings your family customarily makes.Start with Ganesha. He is prayed to first so the rest of the worship goes without hindrance.Worship Lakshmi. Offer flowers, sweets and fruit while chanting Lakshmi mantras.Light the lamps. Place diyas in the puja area and in different corners of the house.Finish with aarti. Sing the Lakshmi-Ganesha aarti and ask for blessings for everyone at home.Families do this in slightly different ways, and that’s fine. Customs vary by region, and many households follow what their grandparents did. The common thread is welcoming prosperity with gratitude, in a calm and clean home.Important mantras and their meaningsMantras give the mind something to hold onto during prayer. The ones below belong to Lakshmi Puja and to the days around it.Lakshmi MantraOm Hreem Shreem Lakshmyai Namah॥Meaning: I bow to Goddess Lakshmi, the giver of wealth and prosperity.Yamadeep MantraMrityuna Pashadandabhyam Kalen Shyamaya Saha।Trayodashyam Dipadanatsuryajah Priyatam Mama॥Meaning: On Trayodashi, this lamp is offered to Yama, the son of Surya. May he keep devotees safe from the noose of death and grant them wellbeing.Narak Chaturdashi Deepdan MantraDatto Dipashchaturdashyam Narakapritaye Maya।Chaturvartisamayuktah Sarvapapapanuttaye॥Meaning: This lamp with four wicks is offered on Chaturdashi to please the deity linked with Naraka and to remove sins.Govardhan MantraGovardhana Dharadhara Gokulatranakaraka।Bahubahukritachchaya Gavam Kotiprado Bhava॥Meaning: O Govardhana, protector of Gokul, held up by Lord Krishna, bless your devotees with abundance.Keep in mind that these belong to different days and rituals within the larger festival. You don’t need all of them on the night of Lakshmi Puja. The first one is the main chant for that evening.The five days of DiwaliDiwali isn’t a single evening. It’s a five-day festival, and each day has its own meaning.Dhanteras opens the celebrations. It’s tied to health, prosperity and the worship of Lord Dhanvantari.Naraka Chaturdashi, also called Choti Diwali, remembers Krishna’s victory over Narakasura.Diwali itself is the main evening, given to Lakshmi-Ganesha Puja.Govardhan Puja recalls Krishna lifting Govardhan Hill to shelter the people of Gokul.Bhai Dooj closes the festival by celebrating the bond between brothers and sisters.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: A woman bought an unremarkable black lamp for just €20 at a French flea market; her daughter spotted a hidden signature and the rediscovered ceramic piece sold for €251,000
articles.summary: A forgotten object, hidden in a cupboard for months, turned out to be worth a small fortune, proving that extraordinary treasures can sometimes hide in
articles.body: A forgotten object, hidden in a cupboard for months, turned out to be worth a small fortune, proving that extraordinary treasures can sometimes hide in the most ordinary places. A routine trip to a flea market in northern France has produced an extraordinary auction result after a family’s bargain find was identified as a rare work by a renowned French ceramic artist. The black ceramic lamp, which cost just €20, sold for €251,000, a world auction record for a lamp by its maker. Scroll down to read the interesting story of a black lamp.A bargain purchase with an extraordinary storyAccording to French news agency The Connexion, the black ceramic lamp was bought by the unidentified woman last year at a local brocante, the French term for a flea market selling second-hand and antique items. At the time, little did anyone know that the unassuming piece was something rather valuable.The lamp was then placed in a cupboard in the buyer's home where it remained until her daughter discovered it during a house clear-out. Looking more closely, there was an incised signature beneath its base, giving the name of the artist as Georges Jouve (1910–1964), one of the leading figures in post-war French ceramics, the report adds.Intrigued by the find, the daughter did her research on the artist and came across NEO Enchères, a Paris auction house familiar with Jouve’s work. The family contacted its specialists and traveled to Paris to have their purchase examined, after learning that the auction house had previously sold a similar lamp, The Connexion claims.Authentication uncovers a rare collectibleThe auction house confirmed that the lamp was a genuine Jouve creation, and, crucially, had survived in remarkably good condition. The Connexion reports that, as ceramic lighting pieces are particularly prone to damage over the years, preservation was key to its eventual value.The lamp’s rarity just made it more charming. While the precise number of units produced by Jouve is not known, the specific model is rarely encountered on the market. NEO Enchères had sold just one other example in the previous two years, which had made €104,000. The newly-discovered piece was valued by specialists at €80,000 to €120,000 ahead of its auction that took place on October 29.The fierce competition causes the price to go upThe lamp generated a lot of interest among collectors, with some 10 prospective buyers competing for it. Bidders participated in person and by phone, a sign of the rare ceramic creation’s appeal. The Connexion report said that the contest finally came down to two European buyers, who kept raising their bids until one dropped out. The final hammer price, including buyer’s fees, was €251,000, or about 12,000 times what the woman paid for it. The result set a world auction record for a lamp by Jouve, far beating the auction house’s expectations, the report adds.According to Quentin Charraudeau, president of NEO Enchères, they had a lot of collectors interested but the price went beyond what the thought. Also, the sale highlighted the growing cachet of rare pieces by French post-war ceramic artists and designers.A reminder of some hidden treasuresThe spectacular sale has also renewed interest in Jouve’s artistic legacy and the market for collectible French ceramics. NEO Enchères is currently looking for other ceramic works and lighting pieces by the artist, as well as creations by other French designers from the post-war period. The Connexion reports that the auction house offers free, confidential valuations from photographs, if anyone thinks they may have valuable items.Image Courtesy: NEO EnchèresYou use AI every day. articles.title: In a 2021 Missouri I-270 work-zone trial, a speed trailer flashing red and blue lights produced an extra 2.8 mph speed reduction; 53.5% beyond the base setup
articles.summary: Discover how a recent Missouri study showed that speed trailers with red and blue lights significantly reduce speeds in work zones. Explore the findings on traffic safety and enforcement methods.
articles.body: In August 2021, a stretch of westbound I-270 in St. Louis gave Missouri transportation officials a headache. Motorists were speeding through the work zone between the Lindbergh Boulevard interchange and Dunn Road, where traffic had to follow a lane shift of about 50 feet, the largest on the project and the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT) wanted evidence on which roadside tools could slow vehicles down. MoDOT’s 2020 traffic figures, cited in the University of Missouri report, put I-270 at more than 140,000 vehicles a day, so even a small cut in speed mattered.University of Missouri researchers mounted radar sensors on either side of the work zone and collected data for about four weeks, from August 3 to August 26, while rotating through several speed countermeasures. They documented the trial in the report, Effectiveness of Speed Management Methods in Work Zones, published in October 2022. One of the tools was a speed display trailer that flashed red and blue lights at drivers going over the limit. During the daytime, it produced an additional speed reduction of 2.8 mph, a 53.5% further reduction compared with the base scenario, a result also listed in the US Department of Transportation’sITS Knowledge Resources database.The work zone alone cut daytime speeds by 5.2 mphThe above-mentioned study recorded a daytime drop in average speed from 64.5 mph at the upstream sensor to 59.3 mph at the downstream sensor with no countermeasure in place. This 5.2 mph decrease was attributed to the presence of a work zone and its lane change. Researchers used it as a base and considered only the decrease that would occur after the base value. In the case of the red and blue trailer, the speeds dropped from 64.1 mph to 56.1 mph, with a total reduction of 8.0 mph. The 2.8 mph reduction after deducting the base value represents a reduction of 53.5% of the base reduction. That 53.5% figure does not mean traffic speed fell by 53.5% overall.Active enforcement added 4.3 mph in the daytime, more than any other countermeasureThe same report showed that during the day, active law enforcement, where officers pulled violators over, added 4.3 mph of reduction compared with the base scenario, or 81.7%. Passive enforcement, a police car parked on the shoulder, added 2.4 mph (46.0%), so the red and blue trailer did better than the parked police car. The ordinary speed display trailer provided 0.5 mph (9.9%), whereas the trailer that had flashing speed digits contributed 1.3 mph (24.8%).Compliance and excessive speeding changed in the same direction. With the red and blue trailer, the share of drivers at or below the speed limit rose from 8.2% at the upstream sensor to 20.1% at the downstream sensor, compared with 4.7% and 9.4%, respectively, when no countermeasures were used. Excessive speeding drivers decreased from 70.2% to 38.8% in comparison with 73.2% to 52.7%, respectively, whereas 92.8% of all vehicles exceeded the limit.The trailer with red and blue lights ran for just nine hoursThat 2.8 mph result rests on a short run, because the red and blue trailer was in place for only nine hours of the roughly four weeks of field data collection. The report’s actual field schedule lists the trailer on August 23, 2021, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., after equipment problems limited its availability. During this period, there were still 28,615 cars passing upstream and 24,117 cars passing downstream, while the effect size of the trailer was 0.83 and considered large. At night, the field test was conducted using the vehicle equipped with flashing red and blue lights instead of the trailer. Because weather and equipment availability kept the trailer out of the field after dark, the nighttime version was tested only in a driving simulator.A 50-driver simulator showed a smaller daytime effectIn the daytime simulations, the red and blue trailer added only 0.4 mph, or 12.6%, which the researchers classed as a small effect. The speed profile seemed favourable for their trailer. At the trailer location, it had an average speed of 50.2 mph compared to 52.5 mph for the base scenario. However, the highest difference, 3.3 mph, was observed 250 feet downstream. The biggest gap with the base scenario, 3.3 mph, appeared 250 feet downstream. By 1,000 feet downstream, though, drivers passing the red and blue trailer were travelling faster than those passing the plain speed trailer. Response to the service suggested something different. The red and blue trailer was perceived to be more effective in reducing speed, but the drivers believed that they would reduce speed more due to police presence.Oregon night paving trials also tested flashing lightsFlashing lights were also tested outside Missouri. A separate study, Effects of Flashing Blue Lights Mounted on Paving Equipment on Vehicle Speed Behavior in Work Zones, appeared in the Journal of Construction Engineering and Management in 2021. Oregon researchers mounted flashing blue lights on paving equipment during nighttime work on three case study projects. At distances upstream of the paver where drivers could see and react to the lights, mean speeds were 4.3 to 25.7 km/h lower with the lights on than with them off. The speed differential, meaning the speed before the work zone minus the speed inside it, was also 4.8 to 11.3 km/h greater with the lights on. The Missouri researchers suggested that some work zones could add a second countermeasure 250 to 500 feet downstream from the first, to discourage drivers from speeding up again after passing it, as mentioned in the above study.You use AI every day. articles.title: Industrial growth squeezing Gujarat fishers off shore, say community leaders
articles.summary: Gujarat fishers warn industrial growth is shrinking shoreline access, citing CRZ violations and delayed CZMPs; seek legal protection and clear small-scale fisher definition.
articles.body: Gandhinagar: Industrial development along Gujarat’s coastline is increasingly squeezing traditional fishing communities out of their spaces on land, with violations of Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) norms and delays in finalising Coastal Zone Management Plans (CZMPs) emerging as major threats to their livelihoods, fishermen’s representatives have told Union govt.The concerns were raised during a community consultation held in Mangrol recently as part of the process to formulate the National Plan of Action (NPOA) for sustainable fisheries and implement the voluntary guidelines for small-scale fishers (VG-SSF). More than 100 representatives of traditional, motorised and mechanised fishing communities, including women, from Gujarat’s coastal districts participated in the exercise.“Fishermen put forth their argument that industrial expansion along the shoreline was eating into the space available to fishing communities, while activities such as line trawling in near-shore waters and discharge of industrial effluents were damaging marine resources,” said the president of a fishermen’s association who was part of the deliberations. Fishermen also called for stricter enforcement of CRZ regulations, protection against displacement and preferential access to fishing resources.Another key recommendation was to clearly define who qualifies as a small-scale fisher (SSF) under the proposed national framework. “While participants did not arrive at a single definition, there was unanimity that deep-sea fishing vessels exceeding 24 metres in overall length and purse-seiners should not be included in the small-scale fishing category,” said a source.The participants also emphasised that the NPOA should cover not just boat owners but everyone directly engaged in fishing and allied activities, including migrant workers employed on fishing vessels.Damodar Chamodia, president of the Mahavir Machimar Sahakari Mandali, Mangrol, which facilitated the consultation, said that a large number of fishermen, representing associations from Jafrabad to Beyt Dwarka, participated in the meeting. “We put forth our representations to the authorities and hope our recommendations will be included in the NPOA,” he said.According to official sources, there are about 5.50 lakh fishermen in the state, of whom over 2.50 lakh are active fishermen residing in over 1,000 villages along the state’s coastline. articles.title: Group builds home for struggling family in Bantwal
articles.summary: Ashaktha Kutumba Seva Yojana builds Rs 9 lakh home for struggling Bantwal family with dwarfism, using pooled donations, weekly collections and labour.
articles.body: Mangaluru: A home is more than just a roof over one’s head, and for a financially distressed family in Bantwal, that dream has finally come true, thanks to the collective efforts of a group of people who turned small individual contributions into a life-changing act of compassion.The family of Lingappa Moolya moved to their newly built Tudar House in Sajipa Hoige Majalu of Bantwal taluk recently, after living in a dilapidated tiled-roof house while struggling to make ends meet. Both Lingappa and his son, Chaitanya Kumar, have dwarfism. Another son, who had the same condition, died during childhood.Lingappa’s difficulties were compounded by an accident in which he fractured his legs, leaving him unable to work. He had previously been involved in small businesses, including running an eatery.Understanding the family’s circumstances, members of the Ashaktha Kutumba Seva Yojana came together to rebuild their house. The construction, which began eight months ago, was completed with contributions from members, weekly collections, voluntary labour and support from donors.The house, built at a cost of around Rs 9 lakh to Rs 9.5 lakh, was handed over to the family recently.Yashwanth Deraje, a member of the initiative, said the group was formed after its members, who had individually been helping financially distressed families through food, financial assistance and house repairs, decided to pool their efforts. Around 140 members have joined the initiative, which brings together people from Sajipa Nadu and Padu villages.The group also supports extremely poor families with essential food supplies. Members contribute one to five kg of rice every month, enabling the group to distribute around 30 kg of rice each to five or six needy families. The initiative has been functioning for about a year, and members do not insist on large contributions, encouraging people to participate according to their capacity.Deraje said the completion of the house has encouraged more people to join the initiative. The group has already received requests for assistance from two more families from Sajipa — one person is blind and the other a disabled man — and hopes to extend similar support to them.Stay updated with the latest Mangaluru news. articles.title: An Ohio man bought a house in 2012, six years before getting married; when his wife argued shared mortgage payments made it marital property, appeals judges let him keep it and upheld a $20,000 legal-fee award
articles.summary: An Ohio man has been allowed to keep sole ownership of a house he bought six years before getting married.
articles.body: An Ohio man has been allowed to keep sole ownership of a house he bought six years before getting married. State appeals judges rejected his former wife's claim that paying the mortgage with shared money during their marriage had turned the house into marital property. The ruling was issued on 6 November 2026 by the Ohio Court of Appeals for the First District. It upheld a Hamilton County Domestic Relations Court decision in the divorce case involving Stephen P. Ellison and Sherrun L. Ellison. The three-judge appeals panel also upheld an order requiring the former wife to pay $20,000 towards her ex-husband's legal costs. The judges said her actions had unnecessarily dragged out the court case and increased the time needed to resolve it. The decision supports existing Ohio property laws on homes bought before marriage, tracking the source of mortgage payments and the rules for awarding legal fees in divorce cases.Financial tracing of premarital real estateThe property dispute involved a house on Elbrook Avenue, which Stephen Ellison bought in 2012. The couple married on 1 September 2018 and lived together for several years before Sherrun Ellison filed for divorce on 11 May 2023. During the trial, the former wife argued that the Elbrook Avenue house should be treated as marital property and divided equally. She claimed that money earned during the marriage and shared household funds had been used to reduce the mortgage balance. However, evidence presented in court showed that after the couple moved out, the husband rented the property to his brother. The brother's rental payments were deposited into a bank account and used directly to cover the mortgage payments. In its decision under docket number C-260069, Judges Bock, Kinsley and Moore ruled that the lower court had not made a mistake in deciding that the house remained the husband's separate property. The court explained that property owned before marriage can remain separate property under Ohio law as long as its ownership and financial history can be clearly traced. This remains true even if the money has temporarily been mixed with shared funds. "The trial court did not abuse its discretion in characterizing Elbrook as Husband's separate property," the judges wrote in their unanimous decision. They noted that the husband had provided enough evidence to show that the mortgage payments came from the rental income kept in a separate account.Award of legal fees and court conductThe First District Court of Appeals also reviewed the former wife's challenge to the order requiring her to pay $20,000 towards her ex-husband's legal fees. During the original court case, the husband's lawyer provided evidence showing that he had spent more than $56,000 on legal fees over two years of active proceedings. The trial court found that the wife's legal arguments and actions had unnecessarily extended the case. This had increased the time and costs involved for both sides.During the appeal, the former wife argued that the lower court had made a mistake by considering statements and actions linked to settlement discussions. She claimed that using this information went against Ohio Evidence Rule 408, known as Ohio Evid.R. 408. The appeals court rejected this argument. The judges explained that while statements made during settlement talks cannot be used to prove who is responsible for the main legal dispute, they can be considered when deciding a request for legal fees under Revised Code § 3105.73(A).The court also explained that Ohio law gives trial judges wide powers to decide whether awarding legal fees is fair. They can consider how both parties behaved during the case and whether their actions increased the time and cost of the legal proceedings. "The trial court did not abuse its discretion in admitting and considering evidence of Wife's conduct during settlement negotiations," the appeals court stated. It therefore upheld the order requiring the former wife to pay $20,000. The ruling fully upholds the Hamilton County court's decision and brings the appeals process between the former spouses to an end.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Photos: Diwali celebrations light up India and its global diaspora
articles.summary: Celebrations feature fireworks, prayers, reunions, rangoli designs, feasting, and the sharing of sweets and gifts.
articles.body:
Diwali, the festival of lights, is being celebrated across India and among its vast diaspora, marking one of the most important days of the year for Hindus.

More than one billion people of different faiths take part in the celebrations in the world’s most populous nation, gathering for prayers, family reunions and the lighting of fireworks.

The name Diwali comes from “Deepavali”, meaning “a row of lights”, and many families place clay oil lamps outside their homes to symbolise the triumph of light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance.

The festival follows the Hindu lunar calendar and usually falls in late October or early November. This year, Diwali is marked on November 8.

While Diwali is rooted in Hindu tradition, it is also observed by Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists, with regional origin stories that share a common theme – the victory of good over evil.

Celebrations often include feasting, new clothes, rangoli floor designs, and the exchange of sweets and gifts with friends and neighbours.

articles.title: Is MAGA losing its grip? Trump's midterm rout sparks revolt within movement
articles.summary: The Republican Party's crushing defeat in the US midterm elections has triggered a wave of introspection and dissent within President Donald Trump's Make
articles.body: The Republican Party's crushing defeat in the US midterm elections has triggered a wave of introspection and dissent within President Donald Trump's Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement, with some supporters questioning his leadership and others debating whether the movement can survive beyond him.The electoral setback has exposed growing differences within Trump's political coalition, which has been a defining force in American politics for nearly a decade. While some supporters blame the president for the losses, others have directed their anger at his advisers, Republican leaders and the administration's failure to deliver on key promises.Trump's policies face growing backlashThe election results have prompted some previously loyal supporters to question whether Trump has become a liability for the movement he built.In Dallas, Michael Little, a 59-year-old businessman and three-time Trump voter, expressed his disappointment after Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton lost. "People are pissed off at Trump. Trump has cost us," news agency Reuters quoted him as saying.Voters' concerns over rising fuel prices, the Iran war and corruption in Washington were among the factors behind the Republican setback. Some MAGA supporters also criticised the administration over the failure to release significant portions of investigative files relating to late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.More than 20% of self-described MAGA loyalists who discussed the results online expressed doubts about the movement's leadership and direction, according to an analysis of social media activity by data intelligence firm PeakMetrics for Reuters. Around half of this group continued to support MAGA but no longer backed Trump as its leader.Supporters divided over movement's futureThe election defeat has also exposed differences over what MAGA should look like going forward. While some supporters want a return to its populist and nationalist agenda, others favour a movement that is less dependent on Trump. A section believes it has already run its course.Steve Bannon, a prominent MAGA supporter and former White House adviser, called for rebuilding the movement by doubling down on its populist and nationalist positions. He also backed Trump's decision to appoint Stephen Miller, the architect of the administration's hardline immigration policies, as chief of staff."Miller's appointment as chief of staff underpins my point," Bannon told Reuters. "There is no more hardcore MAGA proponent than Stephen."However, conservative influencer Isabella DeLuca blamed Republican leaders for taking voters' support for granted and failing to address concerns among younger Americans."Republicans were just lazy. They felt like that they were entitled to people's votes and that people would vote for them no matter what," she told Reuters.She added that the movement had begun to look "tired".Iran war, broken promises fuel angerThe administration's handling of the Iran war and economic concerns have emerged as major sources of discontent among Trump's supporters.An analysis of 12,850 social media posts by PeakMetrics found that nearly a third of posts assigning blame for the Republican defeat cited concerns over the Iran war and Israel's influence on US policy. Another quarter blamed Republicans who were not fully committed to the MAGA agenda.Former national security adviser Mike Flynn described the election outcome as "a massacre" and criticised the administration for failing to fulfil promises on lowering living costs and releasing the Epstein investigative files.Responding to Vice President JD Vance's assessment that the Iran war was "the reason we lost", Flynn wrote: "the sheer number of broken promises is why the blue tsunami happened."Some prominent supporters have also questioned Trump's decision to prioritise the Iran conflict over domestic concerns.Election denial movement faces setbackThe Republican defeat has also dealt a blow to another key pillar of MAGA politics: claims that the 2020 presidential election was stolen.Several candidates who supported Trump's false claims of widespread voter fraud suffered losses in the midterms. According to States United Action, election deniers will hold at least 41 fewer congressional and statewide offices next year. They also lost 70% of the called races for statewide positions overseeing elections.Unlike after the 2020 election, claims of widespread fraud have largely faded from discussions among prominent right-wing influencers following the latest results.MAGA influencer Rogan O'Handley, who has repeatedly questioned the 2020 election outcome, said the Republican defeat was not due to electoral fraud."We lost because we failed to fix the things voters sent us to do," he wrote on X.Can MAGA survive beyond Trump?Despite the growing criticism, some influential supporters maintain that the movement remains central to the Republican Party and will continue to shape its future.Trump ally Laura Loomer argued that the MAGA base would remain essential for anyone seeking the Republican presidential nomination in 2028."The Republican Party belongs to President Trump," Reuters quoted her as saying.However, Christian nationalist pastor Joel Webbon was more critical, blaming Trump for abandoning his supporters through his positions on Israel, the Iran war and immigration."MAGA is dead," Webbon wrote in a post on X.The contrasting reactions underline the uncertainty facing the movement after the midterm defeat, with supporters divided over whether it needs a new direction, a different leadership or aYou use AI every day. articles.title: Eisenkot open to Netanyahu joining Israel’s next government
articles.summary: Israel’s president officially tasks the opposition leader with forming a new government.
articles.body:
Israel’s opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot , the man officially tasked by President Isaac Herzog with trying to form the country’s next government, has said that he was open to including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his coalition lineup.

In a speech at Sunday’s ceremony in Herzog’s office in Jerusalem, Eisenkot suggested Netanyahu’s far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich was also welcome to join.

“If members of Likud and the Religious Zionist Party truly believe this is a time for unity, as they told the president, I cannot conceive of any reason why they would not support a government under my leadership and the principles I have presented,” Eisenkot said.

Eisenkot, who ran as Netanyahu’s main rival, has six weeks to form a new government. At the ceremony, Eisenkot said he will act in the interests of the public and represent all parts of Israeli society.

Herzog, meanwhile, warned that the country faced uncertainties after the November 3 midterm elections in the United States, which brought victories for several political figures critical of Israel and the US’s military support.

“The State of Israel needs a stable government,” Herzog said, pointing to the “new political reality” in the US.

Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and sat as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet for the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.

Despite this, Arab-led parties endorsed Eisenkot for the mandate to replace Netanyahu.

In Israel’s October 27 elections , Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.

Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with the Arab-led parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.

He could also form a government with fewer than 61 seats if he wins a parliamentary confidence vote.

“Netanyahu still has time to derail Gadi Eisenkot’s efforts to form a government and sabotage attempts to gain a vote of confidence,” said Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank.

“In the meantime, he remains caretaker prime minister. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would be the natural second in line to be tasked with forming a government. And if he fails, elections would then be called, and that would still allow Netanyahu to remain as caretaker.

“Many of Netanyahu’s critics say that is his aim. The big question in Israeli politics now is: does the opposition really want to get rid of Netanyahu? Or is the opposition to Palestinian Israelis in mainstream politics so strong that they’re willing to risk keeping Netanyahu in power by going back to the ballot box?”

articles.title: Fast-food chain that once lit up American roads still missed decades later
articles.summary: Iconic fast-food chain The Red Barn once rivaled McDonald's with its Big Barney burger and barn-shaped buildings, but its 300 to 400 locations vanished by 1988.
articles.body: With its distinctive barn-shaped buildings and menu of burgers, fried chicken and other American classics, Red Barn was a pioneer in the fast-food industry. Founded in 1961 by Don Six, Martin Levine and Jim Kirst, the chain grew to between 300 and 400 restaurants before its final locations closed in 1988, according to numerous sources. The first Red Barn opened in Ohio, although there's debate over whether Columbus or Springfield is its birthplace. FAST-FOOD DRIVE-THRUS TOOK OVER AMERICAN MORNINGS FOR THESE KEY REASONS "I think it's important to note that Ohio is actually a bit of an icon as a state when it comes to being the home of iconic fast-food brands," Capri Cafaro, the Ohio-based managing director of America the Bountiful Media, told Fox News Digital. Wendy's, founded in Columbus, was one of the first restaurant chains to offer a drive-thru window, Cafaro noted. It also stood apart from the competition with its square hamburger patties. The roast beef chain Arby's was also founded in Ohio, in Boardman. The barn-shaped buildings of Red Barn restaurants were key identifiers of the brand, as were their comfortable, homey interiors, Cafaro said. PIZZA HUT BRINGS BACK VINTAGE VIBES AS FRANCHISEES EMBRACE NOSTALGIC MAKEOVERS "I think that there is something to be said about matching the aesthetic with the name and making that part of its marketing appeal," Cafaro said of the exteriors. This "iconic material culture" was "pervasive in fast-food restaurants, not just in places like Red Barn, but places like Long John Silver's or, or even more iconically, Pizza Hut," Cafaro said, referencing the hut-style roofs of classic Pizza Hut restaurants. The chain's menu consisted of comfort foods like hamburgers, fried chicken, fish sandwiches and more. A double-decker burger called the Big Barney was similar to the Big Mac but predated the famous McDonald's item, which wasn't added to the national menu until 1968, according to the company's website. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Like McDonald's, Red Barn also used food-themed cartoon characters used as mascots, including Hamburger Hungry, Chicken Hungry and Big Fish Hungry, with "hungry" sometimes spelled "hungery," according to Tasting Table. Red Barn is "evocative of nostalgia and for people that grew up with it." The brand also had a jingle: "When the hungries hit, hit the Red Barn." Red Barn offered a self-serve salad bar, and some publications say it beat Wendy's to the punch. The Wendy's website, however, claims it was the first national chain to introduce salad bars, doing so in 1979. At its peak, there were about 300 to 400 Red Barn locations across 19 U.S. states, Canada and Australia, according to Chowhound. Many factors can influence a restaurant chain's survival or downfall, Cafaro noted. Red Barn filed for bankruptcy in 1986, according to Tasting Table. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS The chain's last 22 locations were in New York, Ohio and Washington, D.C., with the final franchise lease expiring in 1988, Chowhound reported. A few locations were reborn as independent restaurants with a similar feel to Red Barn, including one in Racine, Wisconsin, called The Farm, which permanently closed in 2020. Although not in its original form, The Red Barn still lives on today, with other businesses occupying the recognizable barn-shaped buildings. Red Barn is "evocative of nostalgia and for people that grew up with it," Cafaro said. articles.title: 25 years after Danny Moser was found beaten outside a Wyoming roller rink, his family still seeks answers
articles.summary: Danny Moser was found severely beaten in Mills, Wyoming, on October 20, 2001. He died two days later, and his death was ruled a homicide. The Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation is handling the cold case.
articles.body: There is a phrase Lauren Moser hears almost daily: “You are just like your dad.” It’s something she says she’s proud of, but it comes with weight. Her dad is Danny Moser. He was only 27 years old when he was killed in October 2001. Lauren, who was 4 at the time, is now older than her father ever got to be. Of all dads, why hers? Why did Lauren have to grow up without him? Now, 25 years later, those questions remain unanswered. When Lauren was born in 1997, her family called her Danny’s mini-me. “It was so stinking special,” Danny’s sister, Jamie Haigler, said. “He was so, so incredibly in love with Lauren.” But Lauren says she doesn’t remember her dad. All she knows of him comes from photographs and the stories she’s heard. “From what I’ve been told, I walk, talk, act, sound, exactly like him,” she said. “I don’t have any physical memories.” For Lauren, the loss is as much about the relationship she never got to have as it is about the father she never knew. “I more so grieve what could have been or what I lost,” Lauren said. At 1:04 a.m. on October 20, 2001, a Mills police officer found Danny lying in a pool of blood in the parking lot outside the Wagon Wheel Roller Skating Rink in Mills, Wyoming. He was alone. “When officers arrived, Danny was unconscious, bleeding, and suffering from catastrophic injuries, including severe trauma to his head, skull, and torso,” Commander Ryan Cox of the Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation (DCI) told Dateline. “My mom called me at about 1:15. I was in bed,” sister Jamie remembered. “She said, ‘Something happened to Danny. Meet me at the hospital.’” Cox says Danny was taken to Wyoming Medical Center in Casper, where he was put on life support. He succumbed to his injuries two days later. The Natrona County coroner determined that Danny’s death was a “homicide resulting from severe blunt force trauma to the head.” Jamie says the chaos of that night quickly devolved into confusion. “Everybody was trying to figure out who he was with, what he was doing,” she said. “Why would he even be in that situation?” Jamie is still learning to live with the loss of her only sibling. “We were each other’s best friends,” she told Dateline. She and Danny grew up in Casper and spent a lot of time outside, following their parents around “hunting, fishing, camping.” Their mother loved dogs, and Danny inherited that love. Rarely seen without a dog by his side, he had plans to take over their mother’s dog grooming business. Lauren does remember her dad’s dog, Devin, a chocolate Lab she and her cousins grew up with. “We would actually take naps on his belly,” she said. Devin died on the 10th anniversary of Danny’s death. “That was so freaking special that that dog was so connected to my dad.” But on the night Danny was attacked, he was alone when police found him. And investigators were left trying to figure out how he ended up in the roller rink parking lot. Investigators were able to piece together a timeline of Danny’s final hours, tracing his movements to shortly before he was found. According to a December 2001 Mills PD media release, provided to Dateline by the DCI, “Danny was involved in a verbal altercation at the Sandbar lounge in Casper between 7:00 PM and midnight. Danny was involved in another verbal altercation with a friend at the Cattleman’s Club in Casper between midnight and 12:45 AM.” The release states that surveillance images showed Danny leaving the Cattleman’s Club alone, although it does not specify the time. The club is less than a mile from the roller rink where Danny was discovered at 1:04 a.m. Investigators recovered Danny’s wallet and checkbook near his body. He also had cash in his pockets, “which led investigators early on to rule out armed robbery as the primary motive,” Cox told Dateline in an email. ”Crime Scene investigation indicated Danny was involved in a physical altercation with unknown persons and may have been trying to flee when he was struck by a vehicle,” Mills PD stated in its December 2001 media release. “Suspects and suspect vehicles continue to be cultivated and evaluated, with no definitive results to date.” In the month following Danny’s death, the Mills PD Homicide Task Force identified two individuals wanted for questioning in the case. “Surveillance from the last known location of the victim provided poor quality images of two people, John Doe #1 and John Doe #2, who appear to have been watching the victim and then leave immediately behind him,” a bulletin provided by Wyoming DCI states. The Wyoming DCI took over Danny’s case in 2013 at the request of Mills PD. Twenty-five years later, authorities continue to believe more than one individual was involved. “Based on historical witness statements and physical evidence, investigators have long operated under the premise that multiple individuals were involved in the events leading to his death,” Cox wrote. Danny’s family says he was known to stand his ground, particularly when he’d been drinking. “He was 10 foot tall and bulletproof,” Jamie said of her brother. In reality, that wasn’t true. “My dad was only 5’3” and 100 pounds soaking wet,” Lauren explained with a laugh. Jamie says the friends who were with Danny on his last night have been interviewed extensively. Cox told Dateline the DCI has “evaluated numerous persons of interest and leads” but has not publicly named specific individuals. Investigators hope advances in forensic technology and DNA testing could help identify those responsible for Danny’s death. “Over the years, items of evidence have been submitted for modern forensic and DNA processing; while recent laboratory re-testing has not yet yielded the specific investigative leads we had hoped for, biological and physical evidence remains secured for ongoing analysis as technology advances,” Cox wrote. While investigators continue to search for answers, Lauren has now spent much of her life looking for them herself. “If I don’t keep it relevant, it goes right under the rug, and everybody is so hush-hush,” she said. “I want his name to be known.” She began really digging into her dad’s case when she was just 16. Lauren says she’s spoken with the Mills PD officer who found her dad. “He basically gave me everything that he possibly could as far as information and tried to steer me in the right direction,” she said. “I just couldn’t get anywhere.” Lauren has turned her family’s tragedy into a pursuit of justice. She’s studying criminal justice and hopes to open her own private investigations business. As she learns more about criminal investigations, Lauren says she has pressed the DCI to share more information about her father’s case. “We just cannot get any help or any answers,” she said. In his email to Dateline, Cox acknowledged the family’s frustration but said investigators must protect certain information to preserve the integrity of the case. “The Division of Criminal Investigation deeply understands the Moser family’s pain, frustration, and urgent desire for answers. Our sole objective is to deliver justice for Danny and build an airtight case for court,” he wrote. Protecting information “is the only way to ensure the evidence remains legally viable and that Danny’s killer can be held accountable.” Danny’s family is looking for accountability, too. “If there is someone out there hiding in the shadows that I never get to meet or never get to say my piece to, that’s OK with me,” Lauren said. “But the thing is, someone somewhere has to be held accountable for how long I’ve had to wait without answers.” Jamie says it’s hard living in Casper, the town where she and Danny grew up, where everyone knows what her family has been through. “I would like to see some justice for Danny,” she said. But Jamie sees her brother’s spirit in Lauren every day. And now, Lauren has a daughter of her own, whom she named Danny in honor of her father. “She knows all about her Papa Danny,” Lauren said. “I try to raise her exactly like I was raised, you know, with the memories that I’ve been told.” If you have information about Danny’s case, please call the Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation at 307-777-7181. You can also submit an anonymous tip through the official DCI Cold Case portal. If you have a story to share with Dateline, please submit it here.

articles.title: Before Amazon became a global giant, Jeff Bezos and MacKenzie Scott rented a $890-a-month Seattle-area home; 32 years later, Bezos' property portfolio is worth over $700 million
articles.summary: Before Amazon became one of the world's largest technology and retail companies, Jeff Bezos and MacKenzie Scott were living in a rented three-bedroom
articles.body: Before Amazon became one of the world's largest technology and retail companies, Jeff Bezos and MacKenzie Scott were living in a rented three-bedroom house in Bellevue, Washington, paying just $890 a month, as reported by Architectural Digest. Its garage provided the space where Bezos began working on the online bookshop that launched in 1995. More than three decades later, his property holdings look very different. From waterfront estates and historic Beverly Hills mansions to luxury apartments in New York and a sprawling Texas ranch, Bezos has assembled a real estate portfolio estimated to be worth more than $700 million.The $890-a-month Bellevue rental where Jeff Bezos started AmazonIn 1994, Bezos and Scott left New York City and settled in Bellevue, Washington. Bezos had been working in finance but decided to pursue an opportunity in the rapidly developing internet market. Reportedly, the couple chose a three-bedroom property measuring around 1,540 square feet, paying $890 each month to live there.Its garage provided space for Bezos to begin working on the online bookshop that would become Amazon. Rather than immediately renting a commercial office, he used the available space to get the business moving. Amazon officially launched in July 1995, although its operations soon outgrew the original arrangement and shifted to larger office and warehouse facilities.Jeff Bezos expanded his Medina estate with a $45 million mansionBezos's property purchases began to change as Amazon expanded. In 1998, four years after arriving in Washington state, he spent $10 million on two neighbouring residences in Medina, an affluent community overlooking Lake Washington.The waterfront setting included around 310 feet of private shoreline and a boathouse. The neighbourhood was already home to other prominent technology figures, including Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates.Bezos later invested heavily in the estate. In 2010, he reportedly spent $28 million renovating the property. During the same year, he acquired another house next door, adding approximately five acres to his holdings. The Tudor-style residence measured around 24,000 square feet and had been listed for $53 million. Reports put the purchase price at approximately $45 million.New York apartments added to his growing portfolioBezos began acquiring property on the opposite coast in 1999, when he paid $7.65 million for three apartments at The Century, an Art Deco building on Manhattan's Upper West Side. The three units, covering approximately 4,400 square feet, included a three-storey penthouse and two apartments immediately below it. Their position offered views across Central Park. In 2012, Bezos reportedly added another 1,725-square-foot apartment in the same building for $5.3 million.His New York holdings expanded considerably in 2019. That year, he bought three apartments overlooking Madison Square Park for a combined $80 million. The purchase included a penthouse spread across three floors, measuring approximately 10,000 square feet, alongside two adjoining residences. The penthouse was designed on a scale that went well beyond a conventional city apartment. It included a ballroom, a library with a marble and glass fireplace, a large main suite and a private observatory, according to reports.Two further purchases followed. Bezos paid $16 million for another three-bedroom apartment in the building in April 2020, then acquired an additional unit for $23 million less than a year later. These transactions brought the reported value of his holdings in the building to $119 million, covering approximately 24,551 square feet.Jeff Bezos expanded his Texas ranch to more than 400,000 acresNot all of Bezos's property purchases have been intended as conventional homes. In 2004, he acquired Figure 2 Ranch, a large property near Van Horn in West Texas. The original purchase price has not been publicly established, but the land initially covered around 30,000 acres.The property had previously belonged to attorney Ronald Stasny, who had spent considerable money updating its main residence. Built during the 1920s, the single-storey house underwent changes to its kitchen, bathroom, flooring and porches before Bezos acquired it.The ranch later became known as Corn Ranch and took on a different purpose. It serves as an operational base for Blue Origin, the private aerospace company Bezos established in 2000. Its location and extensive land area made it suitable for the company's work, giving the property a role beyond private residential use.The ranch also has a personal connection for Bezos. He reportedly associated the landscape with memories of visiting his grandfather's ranch in Cotulla, Texas, during his childhood.By 2023, the property had reportedly expanded to more than 400,000 acres. A feature in Vogue, which included a helicopter tour with Lauren Sánchez, offered a look at some of its unusual additions. These included a structure associated with a 10,000-Year Clock, built approximately 500 feet underground, and a bar called the Kármán Line Bar, decorated with space-related memorabilia.A two-storey main residence, swimming pool and several ranch buildings also form part of the property. The scale of Corn Ranch makes it quite different from Bezos's urban apartments and waterfront homes.Beverly Hills purchases included a historic estateCalifornia became another important part of Bezos's property collection. In 2007, he paid $24.45 million for a Spanish-style residence in Beverly Hills. The property included a main house of nearly 12,000 square feet and a separate guesthouse.The estate had seven bedrooms and seven bathrooms, alongside a greenhouse, swimming pool, formal gardens and a sunken tennis court. Its other features included a six-car garage, a game room and an indoor-outdoor bar.Ten years later, Bezos bought the neighbouring property for $12.9 million. The 1956-built house covered approximately 4,600 square feet and contained four bedrooms. He retained both residences.His largest Beverly Hills purchase came in February 2020. Bezos paid $165 million for the historic Warner estate, previously owned by entertainment businessman David Geffen. The property had originally been designed by architect Roland Coate in 1923 for Harry Warner, one of the founders of Warner Bros. Studios. Set across approximately 10 acres, the estate includes a Georgian-style main house measuring around 13,600 square feet, two guesthouses, a tennis court, a swimming pool and a nine-hole golf course. A large motor court and service garage are also part of the grounds.The main residence has several historic details, including antique wooden flooring reportedly imported from overseas. Bezos followed the purchase with another $10 million acquisition in July 2020, buying the neighbouring 4,615-square-foot property.Renovation work continued over the following years. Aerial photographs published in December 2025 showed additions including pickleball courts, a firepit and a beach volleyball court. Images also revealed a metallic structure resembling a spacecraft capsule, while the swimming pool had undergone changes of its own.Two Washington mansions became one major projectBezos also established a significant presence in the US capital. In late 2016, he spent $23 million on two adjoining mansions in Washington, DC, with a combined floor area of approximately 27,000 square feet.The Georgian-style buildings date back to 1914 and had previously housed the Textile Museum. Their size made them among the largest residential properties in the city. Bezos reportedly intended to combine the two structures into a single family residence.Plans for the renovation included a reported $12 million investment in 2018, with proposals for a garden room among the changes. The combined property was described as having 10 bedrooms and 11 bathrooms.In 2020, Bezos purchased another house across the street for approximately $5 million. The additional property provided further separation from the surrounding neighbourhood while adding to his Washington holdings.Hawaii brought a different kind of waterfront propertyOne of Bezos's other major purchases in 2020 took him to Maui, Hawaii. He acquired a compound near La Perouse Bay, reportedly valued at around $78 million. At the time, the transaction was described as a record for the island's most expensive residential property sale.The arrangement was unusual because Bezos bought the company holding the land rather than purchasing the property directly. The site covers approximately 14 acres and includes a main residence measuring 4,500 square feet, with three bedrooms and three bathrooms.Two guesthouses provide additional accommodation, while an outdoor kitchen and a 700-square-foot swimming pool overlook the surrounding coastal landscape. The property also includes access to a two-acre deeded cove.Its position beside the Pacific Ocean and private beach distinguishes it from the urban residences in his collection. The Hawaiian compound remains another example of how widely Bezos's property interests have spread.Miami became his main base after leaving SeattleBezos's move towards Florida became public in late 2023, when he announced plans to relocate from Seattle to Miami. The decision coincided with a series of purchases on Indian Creek Island, a privately developed barrier island known for its concentration of wealthy residents.The location is often called Billionaire Bunker. Among its high-profile property owners are Mark Zuckerberg, Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner, Tom Brady and David Guetta.Bezos began building his presence there in August 2023, paying $68 million for a waterfront estate covering approximately 2.8 acres. The existing residence, originally constructed in 1965, measured around 9,300 square feet and contained three bedrooms and three bathrooms.Just two months later, he acquired the neighbouring Mediterranean-style mansion for another $79 million. At approximately 19,000 square feet, it was considerably larger, with seven bedrooms and 14 bathrooms. A third purchase followed in April 2024. Bezos paid $90 million for another residence on the island, bringing his reported spending on Indian Creek properties to $237 million. The third house covers around 12,000 square feet and has six bedrooms and nine bathrooms.From an $890 rental to a portfolio worth more than $700 millionThe distance between Bezos's first Bellevue rental and his current property collection is considerable. The $890 monthly home was a three-bedroom house where a garage provided the working space for a new online business. His later purchases include historic estates, large city apartments, private waterfront compounds and thousands of acres of Texas land.His move to Miami has changed where he spends much of his time, but it has not meant abandoning every earlier property. He continues to maintain holdings in several locations, including Seattle, California, Washington, DC, New York, Texas and Hawaii.The estimated value of his real estate portfolio now exceeds $700 million. That figure sits alongside a business career that began with an online bookshop launched in 1995 and developed into one of the world's largest technology and retail companies.Disclaimer: This article is based on information publicly available. The Times of India has not independently verified the property details, purchase price, sale price or transaction circumstances mentioned.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Ukrainian nuclear plant switches to generators after losing final power line
articles.summary: A Ukrainian nuclear plant switched to generators after losing its final external power line, though the cause of the latest disconnection is still unknown. “The Zaporizhzhya Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) has once again lost all off-site power, forcing it to rely on emergency diesel generators for reactor cooling and other essential nuclear safety and security…
articles.body:
A Ukrainian nuclear plant switched to generators after losing its final external power line, though the cause of the latest disconnection is still unknown.

“The Zaporizhzhya Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) has once again lost all off-site power, forcing it to rely on emergency diesel generators for reactor cooling and other essential nuclear safety and security functions,” the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) wrote on social platform X .

The plant’s last power line, Ferosplavna-1, stopped working early on Sunday but “the cause and location of the latest disconnection are not yet known.”

“It is the 27th such event during the conflict, underlining the continued precarious nuclear safety situation,” Rafael Mariano Grossi, director general of IAEA, said in the statement.

IAEA said they were told by ZNPP that there were enough fuel reserves to operate a limited number of emergency diesel generators for around two weeks. Grossi called to raise the amount of diesel fuel reserves at ZNPP and stressed the need for the plant to be reconnected with the grid.

This comes after Russian air strikes reportedly killed 55 people in one town in the Zaporizhzhia region, the same region the power plant is located, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Zelensky continued that Russian strikes had also hit vital energy infrastructure throughout Ukraine, leaving 600,000 people in Dnipro, Ukraine, without power. He had previously warned that Russia has sought to launch new strikes that would target Ukraine’s “ energy and logistics .”

“In total, this past week alone, Russia has launched 115 missiles of various types, nearly 1,900 guided aerial bombs, and more than 3,000 attack drones against our cities and communities. These are combined strikes involving many ballistic missiles,” he expressed.

He urged other European and G7 countries to heighten or enact sanctions against Russia, saying “the missiles must be stopped on the production lines.”

U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff announced earlier this month that the U.S. would mediate talks between Ukraine and Russia. The trilateral peace negotiations are slated for Nov. 10-11 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

“Discussions will focus on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and next steps toward peace,” Witkoff wrote in a post.

President Trump has expressed a desire to end the Russia-Ukraine war, which is approaching its five-year mark since Russia invaded the European country.

articles.title: From north to south Kolkata, holy night least silent in recent times; hospitals reel under noise assault
articles.summary: Kolkata Diwali night saw widespread banned high-decibel crackers beyond the 8–10pm window, 11 arrests, 50kg seized, and PM2.5 and noise spikes near hospitals.
articles.body: Kolkata: The city reeled under one of its worst noise assaults in recent times on Diwali night, as banned high-decibel crackers were burst across neighbourhoods well beyond the permitted 8pm-10pm window, with violations continuing into the early hours.Many localities had endured a similar spell of relentless cracker-bursting on the eve of Kali Puja, too.Eleven persons were arrested till 8.30pm on Sunday for bursting banned firecrackers. Around 50kg of illegal crackers were seized in the evening.The state pollution control board (PCB) had received 14 complaints by 9.30pm on Sunday, compared to only four on Saturday. Sources said the complaints were mostly from Haridevpur, Baguiati, Sonarpur, Phoolbagan, Kasba, Patuli, Golf Green and Taltala. A source said five PCB teams reported noise norm violations from across the city.Naba Datta, secretary of Sabuj Mancha, which works for the protection of the environment, said they had come across firecracker explosions on the RG Kar Medical College and Hospital premises on Sunday evening. “The noise levels were above 80 decibel at RG Kar and about 100 decibel at Dr BC Roy Children’s Hospital in the evening,” he said. The ambient noise level in hospitals should not cross 40 decibel after sundown.The noise pollution was compounded by a sharp fall in the city’s air quality. Hourly data from Saturday evening till Sunday morning showed Salt Lake’s PM2.5 level rising from 117 at 4pm to 330 at 11pm and peaking at 336 at 1am. It rose from 148 to 321 in Ballygunge and 159 to 326 in Jadavpur between 4pm and 11pm on Saturday. At Fort William, PM2.5 rose from 120 at 4pm on Saturday to 268 at 1am on Sunday. Rabindra Bharati University recorded a PM 2.5 level of 265 at 3pm on Saturday, while it reached 233 around 3am on Sunday at Victoria Memorial.PM2.5 between 201 and 300 is considered poor, and between 301 and 400, very poor.The barrage began soon after 8pm, intensified sharply after 10pm and continued all over the city till early hours. In many places, the sound demon started rearing its head even before 8pm. Chocolate bombs and other high-decibel fireworks were set off repeatedly in residential localities, including areas close to hospitals and other silent zones. While police action was visible in some pockets, residents across Kolkata said enforcement was lax.Among the worst-affected areas were New Alipore, Golf Green, Kalighat, Garia, Kasba and Sarsuna in south Kolkata; Taltala, Girish Park and Jorabagan in central Kolkata; and Kankurgachhi, Maniktala, Nagerbazar, Sinthee, Ultadanga, Lake Town, Bangur Avenue, Baguiati, Narkeldanga and Kestopur in the north and on northeastern fringes.Residents reported indiscriminate cracker bursting from upscale Wood Street, Theatre Road, Minto Park, Ballygunge Circular Road, Chakraberia and Lansdowne. Residents off EM Bypass, near Mukundapur, Salt Lake, Amherst Street, College Street, Kasba and Golf Green said they heard continuous sounds of firecracker explosions.“I live with elderly parents. A group of men was bursting chocolate bombs just outside my home. I pleaded with them to stop, but they paid no heed. I called police. By the time a jeep arrived, they had left. But they were back as soon as the cops left,” said Aditya Roy, a resident of Sinthee.“I take sleeping pills at night. Yet, for the past two nights, I was unable to sleep. On Saturday night, the torture continued till 3am,” said Rupsa Saha, who lives in an apartment beside Manipal Hospital in Dhakuria.The impact was also visible on animals and birds. “Dogs and cats were running helter-skelter, while frightened birds suddenly took flight after midnight as crackers continued exploding,” said Animesh Bhattacharya, a resident of Garia.Hospitals were not spared. On Kali Puja-eve, the ambient noise level reached 72.7 decibel at RG Kar hospital around midnight and 58.2 decibel at SSKM Hospital around 12.30am.Central Pollution Control Board prescribes an ambient noise ceiling of 45 decibel for residential areas between 10pm and 6am. articles.title: Greenford unveils thousands of orange poppies honouring Indian soldiers on Remembrance Sunday
articles.summary: Greenford in west London marked Remembrance Sunday with a distinctive community tribute recognising the contribution and sacrifice of Indian servicemen,
articles.body: Greenford in west London marked Remembrance Sunday with a distinctive community tribute recognising the contribution and sacrifice of Indian servicemen, Sikh soldiers and millions of Commonwealth personnel who served alongside British and Allied forces during the First and Second World Wars.The centrepiece of the commemorations was a spectacular cascade of thousands of hand-knitted orange poppies, inspired by the Indian marigold, displayed alongside traditional red poppies to form an elaborate Poppy Curtain. Individually knitted by volunteers over several months, the installation brought together communities to remember those whose wartime contributions have not always received the recognition they deserve.The initiative was conceived and led by Greenford resident Amarjit Jammu, with support from Sikh women, the KY Knitting Group, local volunteers and the Royal British Legion Greenford, in partnership with Tracy Green.The introduction of orange poppies was particularly significant, reflecting the growing recognition of soldiers from the Indian subcontinent and the wider Commonwealth whose service and sacrifice helped shape Britain's wartime history.Jammu said the inspiration came two years ago when she attended the Unison Retired Members Conference in Llandudno, North Wales. She was impressed by the extensive poppy installations displayed across the town and wanted to bring a similar community-led tribute to Greenford.“As a lifelong resident of Greenford, I feel immensely proud to see our community come together in such a meaningful act of remembrance. What makes this tribute especially moving is that it has been created by Sikh women whose families understand the true meaning of service and sacrifice,” she said.“When I look at this curtain of poppies, I do not simply see a display. I see the faces of those who served, the families who waited for loved ones to return, and the generations who have carried their memories forward.”The significance of recognising Indian soldiers was also highlighted at Liverpool's Remembrance Sunday service at the Cenotaph outside St George's Hall, where Dr Shiv Pande, representing the Indo-British Association, laid two wreaths.Attended by the Lord-Lieutenant of Merseyside, MPs, the Lord Mayor, political party leaders, veterans and other dignitaries, the service held particular significance for Pande, who said he had been paying tribute and laying wreaths for the past 22 years.This year, he laid one wreath on behalf of the Indian community in memory of all soldiers who lost their lives in conflict. A second wreath was dedicated specifically to Indian soldiers who served Britain during the two World Wars. Pande described it as the first such dedicated wreath-laying anywhere in the UK.Highlighting the scale of India's contribution, he said approximately 1.3 million Indian personnel served during the First World War and 2.5 million during the Second World War. Around 75,000 and 87,000 respectively lost their lives.Back in Greenford, Tracy Green of the Royal British Legion Greenford praised the volunteers and community groups whose collective efforts brought the Poppy Curtain to life.“It has been wonderful to see so many people from different backgrounds, faiths and generations come together in the true spirit of remembrance,” she said.“Together, we have created something that not only honours the fallen but also celebrates diversity, unity and community spirit. We hope this display will inspire reflection and remembrance for many years to come.”As the orange poppies stood alongside the traditional red, the message from Greenford's community-led tribute was clear: remembrance must embrace every community whose people served and sacrificed.As Jammu put it, “Greenford is not changing the story of Remembrance; it is helping to tell the whole story.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Nvidia opens investigation after reports CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence
articles.summary: The board of Nvidia on Sunday said that it was opening an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.
articles.body: The board of Nvidia on Sunday said that it was opening an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The announcement followed reporting by The New York Times and the Financial Times about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese business woman whom the outlets reported had been recruited to spy for China. The two are not related. NBC News has not confirmed either report and has reached out to the Trump administration for comment. “The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company said in a statement. “A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.” The company added that it “has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.” In memo to Nvidia employees shared by the company with NBC News, Huang said: “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.” The New York Times and the Financial Times reported that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen whose Singapore-based company was buying Nvidia’s advanced chips, had been under surveillance by U.S. intelligence agencies. Those agencies, the reports said, found that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China’s top intelligence agency. Jensen Huang and Nvidia, for years, have been at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom. Nvidia’s products are the most highly-sought after chips in the world, however its top-tier products are mostly restricted from being sold to customers in China due to national security fears. China has long sought to become a global leader in AI. President Xi Jinping set a 2030 deadline to surpass the capabilities of American AI systems. Huang, 63, essentially serves as an ambassador for the industry, regularly appearing alongside the likes of President Donald Trump, King Charles, and at conferences to tout his company and what he says will be immense payoff in the future from AI. In October, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, one of the nation’s highest honors for achievement in science and technology. Nvidia is the world’s second largest publicly traded company as of Friday, worth nearly $4.5 trillion. That’s up more than 500% over the last five years. Huang has also seen his wealth balloon leading the company. His net worth has soared from around $25 billion at the start of 2022 to almost $160 billion, making him the world’s 10th-richest person, according to Bloomberg Billionaires Index. In the latest series of these reports, published on Sunday afternoon by the New York Times, the paper reported that concerns inside the U.S. government about Alice Huang and Jensen Huang rose as high as involving Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Speaking to reporters in Florida Sunday shortly after Nvidia’s announcement, Rubio said, “I just can’t comment because of the nature of it, and I also can’t comment on an internal corporate matter that’s going on with Nvidia.” On Friday, the FT reported that the U.S government believed that Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang. In response to that story, the FT reported that Nvidia declined to comment and said that Jensen Huang meets “thousands of customer executives every year” as any CEO normally does. Huang previously defended his interactions with Alice Huang, describing them as business-related in a recent statement: “Our relationship, our interactions, have been related to Megaspeed, and it was all completely normal and not unusual.” In Sunday’s memo, Huang wrote: “To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.” The email to employees continued: “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.” A spokesperson for Nvidia told NBC News that “today’s news will not slow” the company and that Huang was “committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.” Before Sunday’s announcement, Nvidia and Huang were already facing congressional scrutiny over the reports about Megaspeed and its executive. On Thursday, top House Republicans requested a briefing from Huang about the reports. “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” said Michigan Rep. John Moolenaar, who is also chairman of the House Select Committee on China. “It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk,” a letter to Nvidia read.
